target.title: fix(heartbeat): preserve agent identity in global-scope heartbeat context
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With `session.scope: "global"`, a secondary agent heartbeat could silently execute as the default agent. The shared persisted key (`global`) lost the selected agent identity, so the heartbeat could read the wrong workspace and HEARTBEAT.md. A one-line context fix restored the model identity, but deeper review found that storage, process-local reply lanes, and queued system events could still use default-agent or shared runtime ownership.

This PR now fixes the whole boundary:

- preserves the selected `AgentId` in the heartbeat message context;
- keeps global persistence in the selected agent's own session store;
- separates the persisted global key from process-local runtime ownership, agent-scoped for separate stores and shared when agents intentionally share one store;
- agent-scopes global cron/system-event queues while retaining default-agent legacy queue draining;
- covers concurrent global heartbeats so two agents no longer suppress or steer each other.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #99912
- Supersedes the partial approaches in #99941 and #100980
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause and Best Fix

The persisted global key is intentionally `global`, but it is not sufficient process-local ownership for a multi-agent runtime. Deriving the agent from that key fell back to the default agent. Reusing the same key for reply-run registries, embedded lanes, and event queues also allowed independent agents to collide.

The clean fix is to keep the public/persisted key unchanged while carrying agent identity explicitly and deriving a private agent-scoped runtime key. Persisted session lifecycle checks still use `global`; runtime admission, queueing, steering, and heartbeat event ownership use `agent:<agentId>:global`. No config, protocol, or plugin API changes are introduced.

## Evidence

Exact improved head: `8ca46b14779`

### Focused Testbox proof

Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx2nzbcx5xq805ee7ccp0yxk` ([run 28996584887](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28996584887)):

```console
pnpm test \
  src/infra/heartbeat-runner.identity.test.ts \
  src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts \
  src/infra/event-session-routing.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts

Test Files  6 passed (6)
Tests       142 passed (142)

pnpm build
[build-all] phase timings: total 80.0s
exit=0
```

The focused coverage proves:

- secondary-agent identity and workspace under global scope;
- selected-agent session-store ownership;
- distinct runtime keys for concurrent persisted `global` turns;
- one shared runtime lane for agents intentionally configured onto the same physical global store;
- agent-scoped queued and immediate cron events;
- agent-scoped wake consumption even when runtime ownership is shared;
- default-agent legacy global event draining;
- unchanged default/unset heartbeat behavior.

### Real Gateway end-to-end proof

The same exact head was built and run as a real Gateway on Testbox, with two configured agents, separate workspaces and heartbeat files, `session.scope=global`, a real `openclaw system event --mode now --session-key agent:historian2:main` CLI call, and the repository's mock OpenAI HTTP provider. The model request contained only the selected agent's markers:

```json
{"sessionScope":"global","dmScope":"per-channel-peer","requestedSessionKey":"agent:historian2:main","modelSawHeartbeatMarker":true,"modelSawHistorianWorkspace":true,"modelSawMainHeartbeatMarker":false}
```

### Broad gate and autoreview

- `pnpm check:changed`: passed on Blacksmith Testbox in 9m48s (type checks, lint, guards, relevant app tests).
- Fresh final Codex autoreview: clean; no accepted/actionable findings.
- Original untrusted fork head was also run secretlessly on sanitized AWS Crabbox before maintainer fixups: 90 focused tests passed.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with global session scope and secondary-agent heartbeats now get the configured agent's identity, workspace, heartbeat instructions, session store, and runtime lane. Default-agent and non-global behavior remain unchanged.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? Yes — secondary heartbeats are constrained to the selected agent's workspace/store instead of falling back to the default agent.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

The persisted global session key remains `global`. The new agent-qualified key is internal runtime ownership only.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

target.title: fix(minimax): apply request policy to media generation requests
target.body:
## Summary
- MiniMax video, music, and image generation now pass `models.providers.<providerId>.request` into provider HTTP resolution instead of silently ignoring configured request overrides.
- MiniMax video follow-up requests now carry the same resolved request policy through status polling, file metadata retrieval, direct video downloads, and file-id video downloads.
- MiniMax music URL downloads now use the same guarded request policy as the initial music generation request.
- Removes the image caller-level hard-coded `allowPrivateNetwork: false` so configured request policy can control private-network access while the default remains deny-by-default when no request override is configured.
- collision check: searched `minimax request policy`, `minimax allowPrivateNetwork`, and `minimax video proxy`; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found for these MiniMax media generation paths.

## Verification
- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/minimax/video-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/minimax/music-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/minimax/image-generation-provider.test.ts` - passed; `Test Files  3 passed (3)`, `Tests  29 passed (29)`.
- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/minimax/video-generation-provider.ts extensions/minimax/video-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/minimax/music-generation-provider.ts extensions/minimax/music-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/minimax/image-generation-provider.ts extensions/minimax/image-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/minimax/provider-http.test-helpers.ts` - passed; exit 0.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo` - passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` - passed; exit 0.
- focused regression coverage now asserts the resolved MiniMax request policy reaches video status polling, file-id metadata retrieval, direct/file-id video downloads, and music URL downloads via guarded fetch calls.
- mutation check: temporarily removing the image `request:` parameter made `extensions/minimax/image-generation-provider.test.ts` fail because `resolveProviderHttpRequestConfig` no longer received the configured request object; restoring the patch returned the test to green.
- mutation check from the original commit: temporarily removing the video and music `request:` parameters made the focused Vitest fail with `expected undefined to deeply equal { allowPrivateNetwork: true, headers: ... }` in both portal media tests; restoring the patch returned the test to green.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: MiniMax video/music/image generation now honor configured provider request overrides such as custom headers and `allowPrivateNetwork` for the active provider id. The actual network-path proof below exercises video and music against a local MiniMax-compatible `node:http` endpoint; image is covered by a focused regression because MiniMax image generation intentionally uses a dedicated fixed regional endpoint rather than the text/media `baseUrl`.

Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout; actual exported MiniMax portal video and music provider builders; local `node:http` server; no third-party MiniMax network traffic; proxy env vars unset for the proof process.

Exact command run after this patch:

```text
env HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= http_proxy= https_proxy= ALL_PROXY= all_proxy= NO_PROXY= no_proxy= node --import tsx scratchpad/minimax-request-policy-proof.mts
```

The temporary proof script was not committed. It configured `models.providers.minimax-portal.request` with `allowPrivateNetwork: true` and `headers: { "X-MiniMax-Proof": "policy-applied" }`, then called the real MiniMax portal video and music providers against the local endpoint.

Observed output after fix:

```text
minimax-request-policy-proof
video_files=1
music_files=1
provider_paths=/v1/video_generation,/v1/query/video_generation?task_id=video-task,/v1/music_generation
proof_headers=policy-applied,policy-applied,policy-applied
auth_headers=Bearer ***,Bearer ***,Bearer ***
```

Evidence after fix: the local endpoint received configured request headers on the actual video submit request, video poll request, and music generation request, and both providers returned generated media. Additional focused regression coverage verifies that the follow-up legs ClawSweeper called out now receive guarded request options, including video status polling, file metadata retrieval, generated video download, and music URL download. The image regression separately verifies the image provider passes the same sanitized request object to provider HTTP resolution and that the final image POST receives `allowPrivateNetwork: true` plus the configured header.
